rule: Owner rule 2026-10-19: every data pull and holder check is a collector. The main session (the session the owner talks to) is the orchestrator: it launches all first-wave collectors that apply to a scan at the same time on the fast agent tier (Claude Code: model sonnet), and no collector waits for another one. Then it starts exactly one synthesis on the top tier (Claude Code: model opus), which first runs the offline assess step (helius_forensics.py assess: saved files only, no network call, no key, 0 credits), so every source reaches the forensics verdict without a collector waiting. When the synthesis needs targeted follow-up reads it returns its follow-up target list to the main session, which launches them as ONE follow-up wave of parallel fast-tier collectors (wave follow_up) and hands the results back to the same synthesis to finish SUMMARY.md. The synthesis never does those reads itself, never launches agents and never hands the reads to the owner. Any new provider, API key, check or network-calling script is registered here, in the parallel lane, in the same change. tests/test_execution_rule.py enforces this. See SKILL.md, sections 'Execution rule: parallel collectors, one synthesis', 'Follow-up wave' and 'Synthesis'.

entries.name: Bubblemaps free web map (browser, required step)
entries.notes: Public page in a fresh non-persistent Camoufox session; needs Camoufox 0.5.x through the repository's launcher scripts/run-bubblemaps-map.sh. The launcher's default script is skills/dlmm-scan/scripts/bubblemaps_map.py in the same repository; BUBBLEMAPS_SCRIPT stays in the command so the map script comes from the same checkout as every other collector of the scan. A non-zero exit means the map was not read: report unavailable with the reason from the .err file (the launcher prints its FAIL line on stdout, so the .json file is then not usable). The map reaches the forensics verdict through the synthesis's offline assess step (--bubblemaps-json); this collector waits for nothing. HS-BM-MEMBERS-T1: after the cluster sizes are read (as before), the same session expands every cluster in the map's Address List (each header's expand toggle only; no login, no new host) and records each member row; a stale map with a pre-refresh cluster at or over 15% (or clusters together at 30%+) also has those clusters' members read before the refresh click and closed again. Bounds: 45 s for both member reads together (measured 6-11 s per read). After a refresh the read waits until the cluster list itself changed and stayed the same for 5 s (at least 20 s, at most 50 s after the click). Members are display only: the offline assess step matches them to full addresses from holders.json and never counts them. They cannot show why the map links the wallets, holders beyond its top 250 or full addresses (the page shows short ones); a linking wallet holds none of the token. Run time: within about 106 s in the worst case (a 100 s run budget bounds the member reads and the settle wait beyond 20 s; the page load timeout 45 s, the 15 s first wait, the pill steps and the 20 s settle minimum are fixed; measured 26-47 s). The JSON is printed only at the end, so the agent running this collector must use a command timeout of at least 300 s (the Claude Code Bash default of 120 s can kill the run and lose the required size read).

output_fields.clusters[].members[]: each member row: rank (or null), shown short address or label (inert), share_pct (or null; share_shown and share_lt for '< 0.01%'), kind holder | linking | hidden (linking_icon wand | clock)
output_fields.clusters[].members_complete: true only when the rows read equal the header's wallet count (holder + linking + hidden rows), no row is missing and the cluster's end was seen; members_note says why not; members null = not read
output_fields.clusters_before[].members: pre-refresh members of the clusters the pre-refresh line would name (only when a refresh was tried and that line could print); members_before_read, members_before_reason, members_before_seconds, members_before_clusters
output_fields.members_parse_ok / members_reason: false with the reason when the Address List could not be read as the known layout; the cluster sizes are read as before either way
output_fields.members_seconds / members_budget_s / mem: time of the final member read, its hard cap, cluster headers the list read saw
output_fields.clusters_list_only: clusters further down the list that the size read did not see (it sees only the rows rendered in the default window); display only, never counted
output_fields.settle_s / settle_list_changed_s / settl: after a refresh: when the read happened, when the cluster list first changed (or null), a note when the cap was reached, and the cap that applied (50 s, less when the run budget is short, never under 20 s)
output_fields.members_before_not_closed: clusters the pre-refresh read could not close before the refresh click; the refreshed size read may then list fewer clusters (the report prints a size read warning)
output_fields.run_seconds / run_budget_s: time from the start (before the browser launch) to the end of the reads, and the 100 s budget that bounds the optional parts

entries.notes: Free and keyless, so on by default under the existing rule (like jupiter_rows): HS-FEES-T1, the free on-chain route to the creator-fee recipient (MadeOnSol's /fee-shares needs PRO, not bought). It reads no other file of the run folder and waits for nothing. Three steps, no per-item loop: (1) one GET /token-pairs/v1/solana/<MINT> on api.dexscreener.com (no key; for the pool lookup only addresses are kept: the quote mint of every Solana pair where this token is the base side; the per-pair 24 h volumes saved for the DLMM share line are described below); (2) the canonical PumpSwap pool for each such quote mint is DERIVED, never taken on trust: PDA('pool', index 0, pool_authority, mint, quote) under pump_amm with pool_authority = PDA('pool-authority', mint) under pump (pump.json migrate seeds); a Dexscreener pair counts only when its address equals the derivation, and the SOL pair is always derived too; one getMultipleAccounts batch on api.mainnet-beta.solana.com reads the mint, the mint's fee-sharing config PDA('sharing-config', mint) under the pump fees program pfeeUxB6jkeY1Hxd7CsFCAjcbHA9rWtchMGdZ6VojVZ, the mint's pump.fun bonding curve PDA('bonding-curve', mint) (its quote_mint at offset 83, default for SOL-paired coins, and complete at 48 name the canonical pool on-chain, so a coin paired with a token Dexscreener did not list is still found) and the candidate pools; (3) at most one more getMultipleAccounts, for the pool the bonding curve names when it was not already read and for a pool coin_creator (offset 211) that is another address: a wallet (system-owned or no account, on the ed25519 curve), a program-derived address (off the curve: not a wallet) or another program's account; a coin creator first seen in that last read is shown as not read (cap of 3 calls), never as a wallet. Decoded from cited layouts (provider-docs current/pumpfun/idls.md: pump_amm.json Pool, pump_fees.json SharingConfig, pump.json migrate; current/pumpfun/publicdocs.md: PUMP_SWAP_CREATOR_FEE_README, FEE_PROGRAM_README, CREATOR_FEE_SHARING, COLLECT_CREATOR_FEE, HOLDER_REWARDS_README, PUMP_CASHBACK_README); every account validated (owner program, discriminator, length, mint, enum and bool bytes, one to ten shareholders, no duplicate, no zero share, shares summing to exactly 10,000 bps, the PDA and stored bump, canonical pool: pool.creator == pool authority); a failed check is unavailable (layout_mismatch) or (mint_mismatch) with the check name, never a guessed recipient. Also read from the pool: is_holder_reward (fees go to holders, pump.fun pays out) and is_cashback_coin (fees to traders as cashback). Hosts api.dexscreener.com (GET, the one documented path) and api.mainnet-beta.solana.com (POST JSON-RPC getMultipleAccounts only) only, https only, no key, no redirects, no environment proxy, 2 MiB and a hard 30 s wall-clock limit per attempt, at most one retry per request after a 429 (its Retry-After up to 10 s, else 1.5 s; the public RPC asks for 10 s); fixed reason codes. It prints one line, ok (...), empty (what was checked and not found: not graduated, no canonical pool for the bonding curve's quote, no bonding curve and none against SOL or the quote tokens Dexscreener listed) or unavailable (<reason>; ...), and exits 0 whenever it saved creator_fees.json; exit 2 means a bad mint or --out. From the same Dexscreener answer (no extra request, host or key) it also saves dexscreener_pairs, the file's last field (DS-DLMM-SHARE-T1): every Solana pair where the token is either side, once per pair address, with pair_address, dex_id (a short identifier, null otherwise, never printed), quote_mint and volume_h24 (null when missing, never 0), plus pairs_capped when the answer held 30 pairs; only meteora_pools.py --present reads it, for the DLMM share line. PRESENTATION ONLY: never passed to assess or to the analysis engine; the synthesis prints the recipient with the offline creator_fees.py --present <RUN> (no network, no key), labelled with identities the saved first-wave files already give (top holder #N from holders.json or holder-analysis.json, dev as MadeOnSol's claim). It prints only addresses, numbers, basis points, flags and fixed phrases (no provider-chosen text). What it cannot see: who signs the claims or cranks the payouts (transaction history; proposed follow-up), where a recipient sends the fees next, bonding-curve creator fees before graduation, non-canonical PumpSwap pools (no creator fee) and other launchpads (not supported); pump.fun's community-takeover instruction (admin_cto_sharing_config) can still set a new config admin after 'admin revoked: yes'. The runtime checks refuse most layout changes, not all (a field inserted mid-struct could move coin_creator); the guards are pump.fun's append-only layouts and the cache-parity test. The bonding curve, pools and every address off the ed25519 curve are named and never called wallets. Shares are of the mint's supply as this scan's analysis collector read it (else the supply minted in the create tx), cut toward zero.
